---
title: "Canton flag labels"
description: "Create Datawrapper-compatible canton labels in R."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Snippet · Helper available: <code>canton-flags-r</code></div>

## Add to a project

From anywhere inside a project created by `dj-new`:

```bash
dj-add canton-flags-r
```

Load the copied helper:

```r
library(here)

source(here("src", "canton_flags.R"))
```

## Use

```r
flag_base_url <- "https://assets.example.org/canton-flags"
canton_with_flag("AG", flag_base_url)
#> ![AG](https://assets.example.org/canton-flags/AG.svg) AG
```

`canton_with_flag(canton, base_url)` is vectorized and produces Markdown-style labels for Datawrapper. Replace the example base URL with a stable, publicly approved asset host. Do not publish an internal or organization-specific asset URL in this repository or a public project.

## Canton metadata

Keep `tamMap::canton_CH()` as the organization-specific source of truth rather than duplicating a canton table.

```r
cantons <- tamMap::canton_CH() |>
  dplyr::select(
    iso2,
    iso4,
    french1,
    german1,
    ita,
    eng,
    order,
    lang,
    lon,
    lat
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(cantons) == 26,
  !anyDuplicated(cantons$iso2)
)
```

The package was checked on 2026-10-04: `canton_CH()` returned 26 rows and 23 fields. `iso2` contains the two-letter canton code used by the flag helper; `iso4` contains values such as `CH-AG`.
